svg.title: Figure 4. Eccentric loads and the secant formula
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) The lever arm of the load about the mid-length section, divided by the eccentricity e, against P over P_cr: the secant result rises from 1 at no load to about 2 at half the critical load and without bound as P approaches P_cr; the simpler amplification factor 1 over (1 minus alpha) is close to it; the dashed line at 1 is what superposition without deflection (Eq. 4.58 or Eq. 10.37) assumes. (b) For 6061-T6, the load at first yield divided by P_cr against the eccentricity ratio e c over r squared, for slenderness ratios of 50, 100 and 250. For the slender column (250) the first-yield load stays just below P_cr however small the eccentricity, while the linear estimate (thin lines) runs far above P_cr; for the stocky column (50) eccentricity lowers the load strongly and the two estimates are close.
